newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee names Entergy as manager.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee names Entergy as manager.

text.p: Maine Yankee said it signed a memorandum of understanding for Entergy Corp to provide management services to run Maine's only nuclear power plan.
Additional steps, such as plant evaluation and negotiating final terms and conditions, will first be taken befoere Entergy will actually take over management, Maine Yankee said.

Upon completion of the agreement, expected within a month, Entergy will assign a senior executive to serve as Maine Yankee's Chief Nuclear Officer, subject to approval by the Maine Yankee Board of Directors.
Following a full management review, now underway, additional Entergy personnel are expected to be named to key positions at Maine Yankee, the nuclear power plant said.
Charles Frizzle will continue to serve as President and Chief Exeuctive of Maine Yankee until the contract is executed and the Entergy management team is in place.

"Entergy has the experience and expertise to return Maine Yankee to the nation's top tier of nuclear power plants in terms of regulatory and operations performance," Maine Yankee Chairman David Flanagan said in a statement.

The 910-megawatt facility has been taken off line repeatedly over the last two years as engineers corrected problems ranging from cracked steam pipes to safety systems which had key electrical wires accidently removed.
Maine Yankee has extended its current shutdown to mid-February for inspection of the plant's 217 fuel rod assemblies.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent ownd by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro-Electric Co, five percent by Maine Public Service Co and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
